messages:
Claire (Brightline SI): Heads-up: Brightline scheduled go-live in ~12 hours. Their private deployment is failing on two fronts: cluster pods can't resolve `svc.internal.*` over the VPC peering, and calls to the customer HSM-backed KMS key are returning AccessDenied. Need quick architecture triage + mitigation plan. @Jordan P @Maya L
Jordan P: Aware. Quick questions: are you on Redwood Private with managed control-plane or on Dedicated? Also paste a failing curl/dig and any KMS error trace.
Claire (Brightline SI): Managed control plane (Redwood Private). Pod DNS error: `lookup svc.internal on 169.254.169.253:53: no such host`. KMS error from HSM: `AccessDenied: not authorized to use key arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:222233334444:key/abcd-ef01`.
Maya L: 169.254.169.253 is our local stub resolver. Sounds like CoreDNS is forwarding to our stub instead of Partner's resolver for the peered CIDR. First triage: 1) confirm Corefile `forward` targets, 2) confirm kube-proxy / iptables aren't blocking UDP 53 to the VPC resolver, 3) check peering route tables for resolver subnet.
Ravi: For KMS, cross-account grants often fail due to missing key policy statements or mismatched principal ARNs. Ask Brightline to DM the policy + principal ARN. We can also check CloudTrail entry for the failed Encrypt/Decrypt to see which principal was used.
Claire (Brightline SI): Shared CloudTrail snippet in DM: principal arn:aws:sts::333344445555:assumed-role/Brightline-HSM/exec with external-id X-123. Key policy includes a Grant but not an explicit `Principal` statement.
Jordan P: That explains the KMS denial. Short-term mitigation options (ranked by speed):
- #1 (fastest): Create a temporary customer-local CMK and change the service to use env var KEY_OVERRIDE to point at it for go-live. Minimal infra changes, needs ops approval.
- #2: Ask customer to add an explicit KeyPolicy Allow statement for the Brightline IAM role ARN (quicker than grant churn). Could be blocked by their compliance window.
- #3: If wrapping is supported, use envelope key: create a data key under our key, push ciphertext to customer, they decrypt locally with their key. More complicated.
Which do we prefer?
Maya L: For DNS, options:
- Add a CoreDNS forwarder entry to point to partner resolver IP (10.200.2.12). Test locally with `dig @10.200.2.12 svc.internal +short`.
- Provision Route53 Resolver outbound endpoint and create rules to forward `internal.*` to partner resolver (works cross-account but takes longer).
- As a last resort, run a small DNS proxy sidecar/unbound on nodes in the peered AZ that forwards correctly.
I'd test `dig` from a pod first.
Claire (Brightline SI): Testing now: `kubectl exec -it frontend-0 -- dig svc.internal @10.200.2.12 +short` -> `10.10.3.7`. So partner resolver answers.
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0147 - Brightline last-mile DNS + KMS (priority P0). Pager duty: eng-infra and partnerships on-call.
Ravi: Given time constraints, I'd recommend Jordan's #1 fallback (customer-local CMK) if the customer security team can sign the quick approval. We should: 1) document the temporary CMK with TTL and rotation plan, 2) ensure we capture authorization so we revert to the cross-account key after 72h.
Jordan P: I can author the temporary-crypto-exception template and a 1-paragraph note for PMs explaining risk and rollback steps. Claire, can you get customer sign-off for CMK creation?
Claire (Brightline SI): Customer legal ok'd an emergency exception for 48h. They'll create the CMK and share ARN by EOD. I'll also request their infra to allow queries from our control-plane subnet (10.100.0.0/22) to their resolver.
Maya L: Meanwhile I'll prepare a CoreDNS patch that adds `forward . 10.200.2.12` scoped with a `hosts`/`zone` for `internal.` so it's limited. Patch will be a configmap change: `kubectl -n kube-system edit configmap coredns` — I'll test in staging then push to prod if green.
Jordan P: Meeting: 45m quick triage at 20:30 UTC with Brightline, eng-infra, and partnerships. I'll send invite and include runbook link `/runbooks/si-lastmile-dns-kms.md`. Claire attach the CMK ARN when available and the CloudTrail trace in thread.
Claire (Brightline SI): Attached CMK ARN in DM: `arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:333344445555:key/temporary-0123`. Going to open the allowlist request with partner. Will join 20:30 UTC.
Ravi: After go-live we must remove temporary CMK usage, rollback CoreDNS forwards if partner does inbound resolver, and rotate any keys used. I'll add follow-up checklist to the incident.
Jordan P: All right. Action items: Claire - get CMK ARN + partner allowlist confirmation; Maya - prepare CoreDNS config patch and test; Ravi - prepare key-policy remediation; Jordan - draft PM-facing message & runbook steps.
Claire (Brightline SI): Thanks team. I'll update here after the call. :)
